A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of resistance is a complex process that can be affected by many factors, including the environment in which the bacteria grow and the pattern of gene regulation of the infected host.
the fitness effects associated with Rifr Strr mutations are highly dependent on the environment and that the fitness of double resistance can change dramatically when the environment is changed.

double resistance can evolve in the context of phagocytic immune cells, but the fitness cost of double resistance outside these cells may be too large to allow the maintenance of such resistance outside the host.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fitness of bacteria carrying mutations conferring resistance to antibiotics may vary greatly across environments.
the fitness effects and evolutionary dynamics of resistance can be highly complex and context dependent.
the fitness costs of resistance can be highly dependent on the environment and that resistance can be beneficial when bacteria interact with immune cells.
